1.explanation: Both the unminified and minified Ruby language definition files are responsible for tokenizing Ruby source, including regex literals and interpolation. The bug stems from the regex pattern in prism-ruby.js that matches `/…/` literals without embedding the interpolation sub-grammar (`#{…}`). The `%r{…}` pattern is defined separately (and does include interpolation), but the slash-delimited regex rule doesn’t pull in the interpolation tokens. Fixing the issue requires updating the slash-regex definition in prism-ruby.js so that it uses the same look-around and inside grammar as `%r{…}`, which will also propagate to the minified version.
1.bug_scenario: When highlighting Ruby code with Prism, regex literals written with slashes—e.g. `/foo#{bar}/`—do not recognize and highlight the `#{bar}` interpolation. The same interpolation is correctly highlighted when the `%r{…}` syntax is used. In the test page, the tokens for the interpolation inside `/…/` are not separated out and styled as interpolation.

2.explanation: The Ruby language grammar is defined in `prism-ruby.js` (and its minified counterpart). That definition includes patterns for string interpolation and for regex literals, but the slash-delimited regex pattern does not incorporate the interpolation subpattern. As a result, any `#{…}` inside `/…/` is never matched as interpolation. Adjusting the regex literal grammar in these files to include the existing interpolation token will fix the highlighting issue.
2.bug_scenario: When highlighting Ruby code, interpolation inside slash-delimited regex literals (for example `/foo#{bar}/`) is not tokenized as interpolation – the `#{bar}` remains plain text. By contrast, the alternate `%r{foo#{bar}}` form is correctly highlighted with the interpolation token.
